title: Unified title
summary: Nature highlights the advancement of AI-driven frameworks and the importance of climate-related research in addressing global challenges.

facts.statement: Nature's research shows that AI can be used to develop new methods for protein engineering and climate prediction.
The study on synthetic virus-like proteins reveals superior RNA delivery capabilities for cell targeting.
Aquatic invertebrates provide essential nutrients for global populations and contribute to environmental conservation efforts.

sources.title: Retraction Note: Warming accelerates global drought severity
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11027-z

Retraction Note: Warming accelerates global drought severity

sources.title: Connectome analysis of a cerebellum-like circuit for sensory prediction
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10690-6

Connectomics, electrophysiology and modelling of electric fish neural circuits shows how distributed synaptic plasticity across multiple network layers cooperates to enable fast, accurate and noise-robust sensory learning.

sources.title: Designing physics experiments with artificial intelligence
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10898-6

Artificial intelligence in physics experimental design is explored on the basis of searching for optima over a vast space of hardware configurations and proposing entirely new experimental layouts, rather than tuning a handful of parameters.

sources.title: Creating bottom-up RNA transfer vehicles from synthetic protein assemblies
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10952-3

Synthetic virus-like protein architectures designed by artificial intelligence show superior ability to deliver RNA into cells, compared with their naturally occurring counterparts, by overcoming the evolutionary constraints limiting viral evolution.

sources.title: Late-life semaglutide treatment slows ageing and extends lifespan in female mice
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10940-7

Semaglutide treatment for 3 months in female mice improved physiological function, attenuated hallmarks of ageing and modulated nutrient sensors and conserved genetic regulators of ageing.

sources.title: Robust inference and correlates from genetic associations with personality
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10992-9

The genetic architecture of personality is robustly generalizable, minimally confounded and widely relevant to human experience.

sources.title: Pines grow faster and are more drought resilient in the Southern Hemisphere
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10969-8

Non-native conifers from the Northern Hemisphere grow faster and are more drought resistant and resilient in the Southern Hemisphere, where they seem to escape the growth–stress-tolerance trade-off.

sources.title: Rewiring the ribosome to translate proteins encoded in its own RNA
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10962-1

Bacterial ribosomes can synthesize proteins encoded within their own RNA.

sources.title: Molecular mechanisms and pathogenesis of MASH
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10529-0

This Review highlights the state of the art of molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying MASH pathogenesis and its transition to hepatocellular carcinoma.

sources.title: Explainable deep learning improves human mental models of self-driving cars
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10950-5

Concept-Wrapper Network, a concept-based explanation approach deployed on a real autonomous vehicle, improves drivers’ ability to understand and predict its behaviour.

sources.title: Current therapeutic landscape and future treatment perspectives of MASH
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10672-8

The therapeutic landscape and advances in biomarkers for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis are reviewed.

sources.title: The nutritional value of invertebrate aquatic foods
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10908-7

Aquatic invertebrates are exceptionally nutrient dense, supplying the equivalent annual vitamin B12 and selenium requirements for over 5 billion people.

sources.title: Intracellular complement factor H protects neurons during CNS inflammation
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10981-y

CFH is a key mediator of neuronal resilience across the central nervous system in mice and humans.

sources.title: Satellite images before Nepal disaster showed warning signs
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02746-4

Images revealed the accelerated movement of a glacier–rock mass just days before it collapsed, triggering a deadly flash flood.

sources.title: Weight-loss drug slows ageing in female mice
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02468-7

In one inbred strain of laboratory mice, late-life treatment with a GLP-1 drug extends lifespan. This effect might be more than just a consequence of calorie restriction.

sources.title: Aquatic invertebrates contribute substantially to global nutrient supplies
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02541-1

An analysis of the nutritional content of aquatic invertebrate species suggests that their global production is a rich source of nutrients that are crucial for human health. The work provides a foundation for better recognition of these valuable invertebrate nutrients and incorporate them into conservation, management and policy efforts.

sources.title: UN finally admits global warming will shoot past 1.5 ºC climate limit
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02753-5

Earth will breach a long-standing target before the end of the decade, report says.

sources.title: City of slop
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02414-7

Home is where you end up.

sources.title: When do infections lead to long COVID? Scientists close in on triggers and treatments for post-viral syndromes
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02683-2

Hundreds of millions of people have long-term conditions as a result of an infection. Researchers are working out how to help them.

sources.title: Peruvian ice has preserved a global methane record
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02695-y

The first record of global methane in the tropics, collected from the summit of the mountain Nevado Huascarán in Peru, fills a crucial gap in historical methane data sets. It improves our understanding of the contribution of tropical sources to the past and current global methane distribution.

sources.title: Can GLP-1 drugs slow ageing? Mouse study shows promise
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02757-1

Older female mice given an anti-obesity medication lived longer and in better health than did mice not taking one.

sources.title: The death of Jason Arday must prompt deep reflection
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02677-0

Universities and media organizations need to scrutinize their roles in the events that led to this tragedy.

sources.title: Antimatter ‘tag’ used to detect elusive particle decay
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02123-1

A long-underexplored test of particle-physics theory has been revived. This method uses quantum entanglement to infer the presence of undetectable particles.

sources.title: NASA’s Roman telescope holds promise far beyond mapping the invisible Universe
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02764-2

Discovery flourishes when instruments, ideas and people come together in unpredictable ways.

sources.title: Self-driving cars make mistakes, and now users can see why
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02467-8

An autonomous-vehicle system that directly explains its decisions in a way that can be interpreted by humans could improve driving safety.

sources.title: Say hello to the next generation of lobsters — August’s best science images
sources.description:
Nature, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02597-z

The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature’s photo team.
